items.topic: Investigation depth for the next round
items.context: Round 001 produced a broad cross-cutting catalog (9 findings spanning mission, requirements, trust, data model, CLI, API, UI, lifecycle, anti-patterns). The next round can either (a) stay at this breadth and refine wording / fill gaps, (b) drill deep into one specific subsystem where signal density is highest, or (c) widen by walking files this round skimmed (test helpers, cli/internal/support, full plpgsql functions). Confidence is highest on Findings 1, 2, 3, 9 and medium on Finding 5.

options.label: Stay broad — polish all 9 findings, finalize the catalog, lock the conclusion
options.rationale: Fastest path to a usable hand-off for idea/greenfield-vrooli-bridge-foundation-spec; matches the item description (extract signal, not redesign).

options.label: Drill deep into trust/auth (Findings 2 + 3)
options.rationale: Highest-leverage area for the new mission; would produce explicit threat-model anti-patterns the foundation spec can lift verbatim.

options.label: Drill deep into data model (Finding 4)
options.rationale: Useful if you expect the greenfield schema to mirror the audit/history pattern; lower leverage if the new schema is being designed fresh.

options.label: Widen — re-walk skimmed files (test helpers, cli/internal/support, full schema.sql functions)
options.rationale: Closes the medium-confidence gap on Finding 5 and may surface a 10th finding.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide a different direction in freeform.

items.topic: Output format of the final conclusion
items.context: The current conclusion.md is a long-form findings document with prose plus inline lists. An alternative is a compact 'signal catalog' — a single table or CSV-shaped section keyed on (subsystem, item, verdict: keep/drop/avoid, evidence) — that downstream items can consume mechanically. The description names five dimensions explicitly (requirements, trust/auth, data model, UI/CLI patterns, mistakes), which suggests a structured format would map cleanly.

options.label: Keep the long-form findings document (current shape)
options.rationale: Best for human readers and for embedding context into the foundation spec; weaker as a machine input.

options.label: Add a compact 'Signal Catalog' table at the top of Findings, keep long-form below as the rationale
options.rationale: Both audiences served — execution agents scan the table, humans read the rationale; minor extra effort.

options.label: Replace findings with a structured catalog only
options.rationale: Most compact; loses nuance (e.g., on Finding 9 anti-patterns) and is harder to evolve.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide a different format in freeform.

items.topic: Whether to elevate anti-patterns to a top-level conclusion section
items.context: The item description explicitly calls out 'mistakes to avoid'. Currently anti-patterns are split: in-line warnings inside Findings 3, 6, 7 plus a consolidated list in Finding 9. The user asked for 'mistakes to avoid' as a category, which argues for first-class billing.

options.label: Promote anti-patterns to a dedicated top-level section between Findings and Limitations
options.rationale: Matches the item description verbatim; makes the section easy for the foundation spec to lift wholesale.

options.label: Leave anti-patterns inside Finding 9 (current shape)
options.rationale: Avoids duplication; relies on readers scrolling to Finding 9.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide a different organization in freeform.

items.topic: Scope of 'reusable' — does framework / infra boilerplate count?
items.context: Findings 5, 6, and 8 catalog cliapp.ScenarioApp, api-core (preflight/server/health/database), and .vrooli/service.json lifecycle 2.0.0 — all of which every new Vrooli scenario already adopts by default. Recording them as 'reusable signal' is technically true but may dilute the catalog. The greenfield runtime backlog item (execute/greenfield-vrooli-bridge-core-runtime) will pick these up regardless of what this conclusion says.

options.label: Include framework/infra patterns explicitly (current shape)
options.rationale: Defensive — guarantees nothing is missed; useful if a non-Vrooli reader picks up the spec.

options.label: Demote framework/infra patterns to a single 'Conventions inherited by default' note, expand domain-relevant signal
options.rationale: Sharper signal; trusts the existing scenario template to deliver these without explicit reminders.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide a different scoping rule in freeform.

items.text: Mission mismatch is sharp: the legacy bridge solves external-project documentation injection, while the trusted-node-bridge initiative is about Vrooli↔Vrooli node collaboration for remote validation. Of the 15 entries in scenarios/vrooli-bridge/requirements/index.json (VRB-REQ-001..015), zero map to the new mission; only PRD line OT-P0-007 (which is missing from requirements/index.json entirely) does.

There is no trust, auth, identity, or remote-host code anywhere in the legacy implementation despite the PRD listing OT-P0-007. The CLI explicitly sets AllowAnonymous: true and the API CORS middleware is hardcoded to http://localhost:3000. This is the most important *gap* (not signal) to surface to the foundation spec.

PostgreSQL schema (initialization/storage/postgres/schema.sql) has 4 tables (projects, integration_history, project_files, project_tags) plus a project_summary view, integration_health view, an update-timestamp trigger, and an add_integration_history plpgsql function. The general patterns (UUID PK, JSONB metadata, status enums, audit table, BEFORE UPDATE trigger, plpgsql insert seam) generalize; the specific tables do not.

CLI uses cliapp.NewStandardScenarioApp + cliapp.SubcommandGroup with NeedsAPI: true and verb-style subcommands (list/scan/integrate/remove). The shape is the current Vrooli CLI standard — the new bridge will follow the same pattern with different domain verbs (likely node + session groups).

UI is vanilla JS (single index.html + app.js + styles.css) with a static 'cp -R' build. This violates the project's 'every scenario uses react-vite' guideline and will be rebuilt regardless. The only reusable UX ideas are page composition (header / stat cards / filters / list / modal) and per-row action sets — not code.

plan_updates: Created the initial conclusion.md scaffold (~12 KB) with: research question, summary, methodology, 9 findings (mission mismatch, OT-P0-007 inheritance, trust gaps, data-model patterns, CLI patterns, API patterns, UI patterns, lifecycle conventions, concrete anti-patterns), limitations, and three placeholder/likely Actions. No plan.md is produced for research items per the research-conclusion-authoring skill.
